messages:
acme_alerts_bot: alert: ACME tenant 6789 - SIEM shows missing audit events 2024-03-10 01:00 -> 03:00 UTC (2h hole). link: https://acme.siem.example/incident/9876 - urgent, customer-facing.

acme_sre_taylor: we see the same in our ingest dashboard. tenant=acme-6789, export prefix s3://redwood-audit/tenant=acme-6789/date=2024-03-10/ - manifests exist but a lot of event batches around 01:00 are empty. pasted manifest snippet below.

acme_sre_taylor: ```
{"batch_key": "batch-20240310T00-59-01.gz", "events": 0, "size": 0}
{"batch_key": "batch-20240310T01-15-22.gz", "events": 0, "size": 0}
{"batch_key": "batch-20240310T02-05-10.gz", "events": 0, "size": 0}
```

support_jen: thanks Taylor. can you paste the s3 manifest file path + one example object key that you expect to have events? also any request ids from the forwarder logs would help.

acme_sre_taylor: manifest s3 path: s3://redwood-audit/tenant=acme-6789/date=2024-03-10/manifest-20240310.json. example expected object: s3://redwood-audit/tenant=acme-6789/date=2024-03-10/batch-20240310T01-15-22.gz, x-request-id: rq-0a1b2c3d.

mike_eng_security: quick hypothesis: DST/timezone handling rounded event_time into a different bucket at forwarder, then retention/rollup filtered those buckets. two things to check: 1) forwarder logs for KMS decrypt errors (if a batch fails decrypt we sometimes mark zero events), 2) timestamps in the manifest vs embedded event_time values (local tz vs UTC).

eng-infra-bot: forwarder log excerpt for rq-0a1b2c3d: 
"2024-03-10T01:15:22Z INFO forwarder: ingest_batch tenant=acme-6789 batch=batch-20240310T01-15-22.gz events=0 reason=invalid_event_times
2024-03-10T01:15:22Z WARN forwarder: sample_event: {\"event_time\": \"2024-03-10T01:10:45-06:00\", \"id\": \"evt-123\"} cannot_normalize_timezone
"

maria_sre: I checked raw-store (cold S3) for that object: GET returned 200 but object size is 0 for multiple keys. seems the forwarder wrote zero-byte objects. Did we ever see KMS decrypt failures?

acme_sre_taylor: we do have a separate log entry earlier for rq-0a1b2c3d: "kms: decrypt ok" so it's not KMS. The sample event_time above is in -06:00 (America/Chicago) because the customer's sources were in CST and the forwarder tried to normalize to UTC but hit DST transition (spring forward) and computed an invalid bucket.

mike_eng_security: that makes sense. edge case: on spring-forward day some local times (e.g., 02:30 local) don't exist; if forwarder code attempted naive local->UTC conversion it might drop or mark events as invalid. we should treat invalid conversions as UTC-preserve or fallback to event ingestion time.

elena_support: action items suggestion: 1) confirm whether raw events exist in firehose/raw topic (to distinguish lost vs bucketed); 2) temporarily re-run replay job for manifest-20240310.json to rehydrate missing batches into SIEM; 3) add short-term mapping to forwarder to accept local tz and normalize safely. Also we should notify customer about short retention risk.

maria_sre: check on (1): I queried the raw Kafka topic for tenant acme-6789 between 2024-03-10T00:30Z and 2024-03-10T03:30Z - found ~14k events with event_time fields in -06:00, all present. so events made it to raw, but forwarder produced zero-sized S3 objects.

support_jen: useful. so not data-loss upstream. next question: why did forwarder write zero-byte instead of writing with corrected timestamps? is there a retry/backoff that collapsed to 0 bytes on failure?

eng-infra-bot: forwarder error trace: 
"error: normalize_event_times: invalid_local_time -> dropping batch with zero_events_written to manifest. stack: forwarder/timestamp_normalizer.go:142"

mike_eng_security: ok root cause: timestamp_normalizer treated unrepresentable local-times as fatal for batch. fix options: non-breaking patch to mark per-event fallback to ingestion timestamp; mid-term fix to re-run conversion logic to accept tz offsets and compute UTC robustly; long-term add unit coverage for DST edgecases.

acme_sre_taylor: customer is asking for immediate repro/backfill steps so they can show internal auditors. can we provide a playbook?

elena_support: proposed playbook (short): 
1) Run replay job: `replay-manifest --tenant acme-6789 --manifest s3://redwood-audit/tenant=acme-6789/date=2024-03-10/manifest-20240310.json --mode rehydrate`
2) Set forwarder feature flag `timestamp_normalizer_strict=false` for acme-6789 for 24h to let older batches be accepted.
3) Validate rehydrated S3 batch sizes and confirm SIEM reingest success.
4) Patch forwarder: PR -> canary -> cut release.

mike_eng_security: I'll own the patch. owner=@mike_eng_security. ETA for canary deploy 48 hours. I'll also prepare a short customer-facing note explaining root cause (DST edge case) and mitigation steps.

support_jen: I'll run the replay job now (with infra help) and set the feature flag. pinging @maria_sre to confirm rehydrate results.

maria_sre: replay job started at 2024-03-10T18:04:00Z, job-id replay-20240310-acme-6789-01. monitoring.

acme_sre_taylor: thanks team. will update internal auditors once we see events reappear. please keep me posted on the forwarder patch schedule.

support_jen: summary/action items: 1) replay manifest -> in progress (maria) 2) flag change for tenant (jen) 3) patch/ticket (mike) 4) customer comms (jen). I created ticket INFRA-3145 and linked logs.

mike_eng_security: note for postmortem: add unit tests for timezone normalization and add an observability metric for batches dropped_due_to_timestamp_errors.

acme_alerts_bot: customer update: ACME asked for ETA and a copy of the replay records for audit.

support_jen: will deliver audit CSV after replay completes. closing loop in this thread once SIEM shows reingested counts. :thumbsup:
